body.claim: Derives an authorized_action from a signed tool classification fact, so a semantic identity minted from a classified tool call is re-derivable offline from signed facts plus this versioned ruleset and its pinned dependency artifacts alone. Shaped as a ruleset, not a single rule, so a later Permit-to-X (e.g. a deploy classification) is a new rule entry, not a schema change.
body.digest_convention: All digests are lowercase sha256 hex with the 'sha256:' prefix, matching every other permit-to-x artifact. base64 is used only for Ed25519 keys/signatures elsewhere, never for artifact or input digests.

registered_tool.forbidden_fields: fields belonging to other (future) subject variants MUST be absent
registered_tool.unknown_kind_outcome: unsupported_derivation_subject (no_derivation, not invalid): a verifier that does not recognise the kind yields no title, it does not reject the permit.

classification_input_canonicalization.bytes: serialize the logical_object with keel.canonical_json.payload.v1; input_digest = sha256: over those bytes. The profile string is part of the object so two different logical structures cannot canonicalize to the same bytes.
classification_input_canonicalization.purpose: Two independent verifiers computing input_digest for the same call MUST agree byte-for-byte.

identifier_grammar.equality: validate against the grammar, then compare byte-for-byte. No case folding, Unicode normalization, whitespace trimming, alias resolution, or version stripping at verification time. connector_identity is the operator-registered identity produced by the issuer's normalize_known_mcp_connector_identity; canonical_tool_name is the Keel-resolved name produced by normalize_mcp_tool_name; both are already normalized at issuance and frozen into the signed record.
identifier_grammar.malformed: an identifier that fails the grammar makes the binding invalid, not merely unmatched.

resolution.note: exactly_one, never first-match. A future rule that also matched would surface as invalid rather than silently pick one.

predicate_vocabulary.classification_registry_membership: (classification.subject.connector_identity, classification.subject.canonical_tool_name) MUST be an entry in the classification_registry dependency resolved below. Absent entry with an otherwise-valid record: no_derivation.
predicate_vocabulary.classification_registry_digest_match: classification.provenance.registry.artifact_digest MUST equal the resolved classification_registry artifact digest. Mismatch: invalid.
predicate_vocabulary.classification_input_digest_match: classification.provenance.input.digest MUST equal the digest recomputed per classification_input_canonicalization. Mismatch: invalid.
predicate_vocabulary.closed_set: This is the entire predicate vocabulary for v1. There is no general expression language. A permit referencing an unknown predicate is unverifiable, not silently passed.

dependencies.note: payment.execute -> Permit-to-Pay is unchanged from the existing presentation path.

historical_resolution.model: keel-verifier version-aware resolution (keel-verifier v3.7.0): resolve each dependency by the version+digest the permit embeds, NOT by whatever is current. Never substitute a newer artifact for an older permit.
historical_resolution.unavailable: If the exact artifact bytes for the embedded digest cannot be found, the outcome is unverifiable / artifact_unavailable, never a fallback to a newer version.
historical_resolution.resolve_by: algorithm + digest is identity; artifact_id + version are metadata and type checks.

outcome_taxonomy.valid: all applies_when + requires satisfied; authorized_action derived; feeds the existing semantic selector as action_name/operation = payment.execute.
outcome_taxonomy.no_derivation: rule not applicable, subject kind unrecognised, or registry entry absent -> generic title, permit otherwise unaffected.
outcome_taxonomy.invalid: digest mismatch, malformed identifier, or multiple rules match -> the semantic binding is invalid.
outcome_taxonomy.unverifiable: a required dependency artifact is unavailable, or an unknown predicate is referenced -> cannot decide; do not treat as valid or as generic.

invariants: invocation.operation stays call.tools; authorized_action is payment.execute; these are distinct signed facts, never two values of one field.
transport_surface and target_surface are recorded separately. target_surface = payment_rail is the action's resource class, not a claim the wire was a native payment-rail integration.
control.mode == enforced_in_path is REQUIRED. Enforcement qualifies issuance; it does not define the action. An observed call never derives a payment authorized_action.
No provider outcome, settlement, or completion is implied. payment.execute is authority to attempt; observed_evidence carries what happened.
The classification decision bound here MUST be the same one used to enforce, bound by input_digest + registry digest, not a re-lookup that could diverge under normalization.
body.non_authorizing: This ruleset governs presentation identity only. It never affects policy evaluation, dispatch, executable authority, or verdicts. A wrong derivation degrades a title; it cannot escalate authorization.
body.normative_surface: The test-vector corpus keel.permit.action_classification_derivation.test_vectors.v1 is the machine-checkable contract. Two independent verifiers that agree on the corpus conform; this document explains the corpus, it does not replace it.
